cards.explanation: The answer is lies, friends. The LORD says, "Ephraim surrounds Me with lies…" and then adds that the house of Israel does it with deceit. That's a whole crowd of falsehood closing in. Ephraim is the northern kingdom of Israel, and the charge starts right here.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, "but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One." Judah is the southern kingdom, and after all that talk of lies, this one little word "but" lands like a cool breeze in a hot kitchen. Still walking, still faithful. That's what the LORD says about Judah in this line.
The answer is olive oil, friends. Ephraim "…makes a covenant with Assyria and sends olive oil to Egypt." Assyria gets the covenant, and Egypt gets the olive oil. Ephraim has his hands in both places.

The answer is False, friends. The text says, "He will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds." The word is according, so it's tied to ways and deeds. The punishment follows what has been done.

The answer is heel, friends. "In the womb he grasped his brother’s heel…" The man was holding on before he'd even been introduced to anybody. I've got a mustache for hands, and I still wouldn't try that.

The answer is that he weeps and seeks His favor, friends. The text says "he wept and sought His favor…" So the story doesn't stop at the win. The wrestler is crying and asking for favor, and the text also says he found Him at Bethel.

The answer is return to your God, friends. The text says, "But you must return to your God…" After Jacob's story comes that "But," and the prophecy turns. It's a call to come back to God, plain and direct. And I think it lands softer than it sounds, since Jacob wept and sought favor and found Him.

The answer is always, friends. The call says "maintain love and justice, and always wait on your God." Always, not just when it's easy. I set a timer and hover over my oven like it owes me money, so waiting is not my best skill. That's why I like that word.

The answer is True, friends. Ephraim says, "How rich I have become! I have found wealth for myself." Notice it's all I and myself. That's a man admiring his own wallet, and I've caught myself admiring a perfect batch the same way.

The answer is that no one can find sinful iniquity in him, friends. Ephraim says, "In all my labors, they can find in me no iniquity that is sinful." He's claiming a spotless record. And the very next words from the LORD begin with "But," so the claim doesn't get the last word.

The answer is tents, friends. The LORD says, "I will again make you dwell in tents, as in the days of the appointed feast." Notice the word again. It says dwelling in tents has happened before, and the LORD ties it to the days of the appointed feast.

The answer is False, friends. The LORD says, "I spoke through the prophets and multiplied their visions; I gave parables through the prophets." Twice in one verse He says through the prophets, not the kings. When something's said twice that clearly, it's worth remembering.

The answer is heaps of stones in the field, friends. The text says, "…their altars will be heaps of stones in the furrows of the field." The question is about sacrificing bulls in Gilgal, a town in Israel, and it's the altars that become those heaps. Those altars won't stay standing.

The answer is a wife, friends. The text says Israel worked for a wife, and for a wife he tended sheep. Same man as Jacob, since Genesis 32:28 says his name was changed to Israel. Sheep for a wife. That's quite a story.

The answer is prophet, friends. The text says, "But by a prophet the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt, and by a prophet he was preserved." The LORD is the one doing the bringing out, and He does it by a prophet. The same line says that by a prophet Israel was preserved.

The answer is his bloodguilt, friends, and I think this one is heavy. The text says, "…his Lord will leave his bloodguilt upon him…" The line comes after Ephraim has provoked bitter anger. It goes on to say his Lord will repay him for his contempt.
